claims.interpretation: Fixes the operational definition and the rule for missing end times.

synthesis: Seven records retrieved in two recorded searches, appraised at abstract level. Call-log studies consistently show slower notification for outpatient and community results, especially after hours (71 against 94 percent within 30 minutes in one multicentre analysis), with repeated call attempts and unreachable clinicians as the main mechanisms. A single night technologist covering bench work is associated with more delay. Verification time stamps are reliable and read-back times are occasionally missing, which supports a verification-to-read-back interval with missing end times treated as unsuccessful. Escalation pathways are associated with shorter times, but links to patient outcomes are sparse.
gradeRationale: Several large call-log analyses and a review agree on where delays occur, with reliable time-stamp data; the evidence is observational but the question is descriptive. Moderate certainty about the pattern of delays; low certainty about effects of escalation routes.
summary: Seven records from two recorded searches appraised; five source-derived claims recorded; overall certainty moderate.
